newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: O'Connor's says shareholders may change.
newsitem.headline: O'Connor's says shareholders may change.

text.p: O'Connor's Corp Bhd said on Tuesday that it was proposing a rationalisation exercise which could see a change in its substantial shareholders.
Under the proposals, it would transfer all its businesses and assets to O'Connor's Properties Sdn Bhd, the company said in a statement issued by its merchant bankers.
O'Connor's Corp sells telecommunications products and distributes electronic and consumer goods.
The company would then sell a 49 percent equity interest in O'Connor's Properties to O'Connor's Holding Pte Ltd (OCH) for 66.1 million ringgit in cash.
OCH would in turn dispose its entire 51 percent interest in O'Connor's Corp to private firm Great Aura (M) Sdn Bhd for 170.8 million ringgit or about 7.88 ringgit a share.
O'Connor's Corp stock closed Tuesday trading at 8.05 ringgit, unchanged.
The statement did not say who were the controlling shareholders of Great Aura.
It said the proposals would oblige Great Aura to make a mandatory general offer for the remaining 49 percent stake in O'Connor's Corp.
The exercise will enable O'Connor's Corp to retain controlling interest in its existing businesses and assets as well as raising cash of 66.1 million ringgit, it said.
The cash would be used to diversify its earnings base, including manufacturing and long-term infrastructure development projects, especially in marine-based resorts.
"These future projects will enable (O'Connor's Corp) to diversify from its dependence on its present trading activities which are highly competitive, and with eroding margins," the statement said.
The proposals need approval from Malaysian regulatory authorities, O'Connor's Corp shareholders, its parent firm Wearnes International (1994) Ltd, and WBL Corp Ltd, the holding company of Wearnes.
